tip.title: First, next, then, last
tip.text: Events and instructions happen in order. Watch for signal words: FIRST, NEXT, THEN, AFTER, BEFORE, FINALLY. When a question asks what happened before or after something, go back to the text and check which sentence comes earlier. Do not trust memory. Order questions are easy points if you look.

passage.title: First Shift
passage.text:
Rico got a weekend job at his uncle's car wash. He was fifteen. It was his first real job.

On Saturday, his uncle showed him the steps. First, spray the car with water to get the mud off. Next, soap the car from the roof down. Then rinse it, again from the top. After that, dry it with a clean towel. Finally, wipe the tires so they shine.

Rico washed his first car slowly. It took him forty minutes. His uncle checked it and found soap near the mirror. Rico wiped it again.

By the fifth car, Rico needed only fifteen minutes. His arms hurt. His shirt was soaked. At six o'clock his uncle gave him three hundred pesos. Rico folded the bills and put them in his pocket. He had never been so tired, or so proud.

words.meaning: a set time of work, like a morning or weekend shift
words.example: Her shift at the store ends at nine.

words.meaning: to wash off soap with clean water
words.example: Rinse the plates before you dry them.
We were soaked after the rain.

items.prompt: What is the FIRST step in washing a car?
items.why: "First, spray the car with water to get the mud off."
"Then rinse it... After that, dry it with a clean towel."

items.prompt: Put the car wash steps in order.
items.why: The signal words First, Next, Then, After that, and Finally give this order.

items.prompt: How long did Rico's first car take?
"His shirt was soaked." What does soaked mean?
items.why: He had been spraying and rinsing cars all day, so his shirt was completely wet.

items.prompt: Why did Rico get faster by the fifth car?
choices: He learned the steps and stopped making mistakes.
items.why: He went from forty minutes to fifteen after practice and after fixing the soap mistake. Practice made him faster.

items.prompt: Where did Rico's uncle find soap on the first car?
items.why: "His uncle checked it and found soap near the mirror."

items.prompt: How much did Rico's uncle pay him at six o'clock?
items.why: "At six o'clock his uncle gave him three hundred pesos."

items.prompt: "Then rinse it, again from the top." What does rinse mean?
choices: Wash off the soap with clean water
items.why: The step before is soaping the car, and the step after is drying it. Rinsing is washing the soap off with water in between.

items.prompt: The title is "First Shift." Which words in the passage help you know what a shift is?
choices: "weekend job" and "At six o'clock his uncle gave him three hundred pesos"
items.why: The passage is about Rico's job and the hours he worked until six o'clock. A shift is a set time of work.
